_comment: Where each agent publishes the version number its evidence should be compared against.
A null source is not an oversight -- it records that no machine-readable release feed
is known for that agent, so its row can only be re-verified by a human who has it.
Saying so is the point: an invented package name would silently track the wrong thing,
which is worse than admitting the gap. Add a source only after checking it resolves.

aider.note: The pip-installable CLI; the project publishes every release here.

antigravity.note: IDE download, no public release feed found. Manual check.

claude_code.note: The reference row. Drift here matters most: every other adapter was shaped against it.

copilot.note: Release notes repo for the extension; the extension itself is marketplace-only.

cursor.note: IDE download with no public feed. `cursor-agent` exists on npm but has NOT been shown to share the IDE's hook config path -- tracking it would evidence a different binary than this row describes.

devin.note: Hosted. There is no version to pin; the vendor can change behaviour under a row without any observable release.

grok.note: No confirmed release feed. Manual check.

junie.note: JetBrains plugin marketplace. Feed exists but is not yet wired here.

kimi_code.note: No confirmed release feed. Manual check.

tabnine.note: Multi-IDE plugin, per-IDE versioning. Manual check.

windsurf.note: IDE download, no public release feed found. Manual check.
